name: Prize crossword No 23,370
preamble: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: The price includes the house and help at home

indicators.note: to include something is to take it within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the price of something is what it costs
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A household budget where the cost covers both the property and a domestic helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help at home' suggests a cleaner or housekeeper, but the help is given to the host of a party or show in their own home.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-host shares hosting duties, assisting the main host when guests are received at a house.

clue.text: I'm drunk: to frighten lawyer kept my head

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
something kept is held inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them
a silk is a senior barrister, from the silk gown of a King's Counsel
the opening letter of 'my'

explanation.surface: A drunk confesses that his frightening lawyer kept him from losing his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm drunk' reads as a confession of intoxication, but it is the answer speaking: milk is a thing that is drunk. The M slips in after the S of SILK.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk from cows is a beverage, so it can say of itself that people swallow it as a drink.

clue.text: Hospitals keeping lots of heads sans cover

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing heads, as the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: to keep is to hold on to, so the outer piece wraps around the inner one

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital, doubled as a plural
oodles means a great quantity

explanation.surface: Hospital wards are full of patients with bare heads.
explanation.walkthrough: Plural abbreviations are often made by doubling or adding S; here H plus S frames the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood covers the head, so being without one leaves the head bare and uncovered.

clue.text: Cooks taking time - red lights are in these areas

definitions.text: red lights are in these areas

blocks.note: first meaning: simmers food slowly over a long period

blocks.clueFragment: red lights are in these areas
blocks.note: second meaning: old word for brothels or the districts that held them

explanation.surface: Slow cooks wait for food while red lights glow, as in a kitchen or a seedy quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic sense is the one solvers miss: in Shakespeare's time 'the stews' were London's brothel districts, the original red-light areas.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means slow simmering in liquid, while the old plural noun named brothels, the places where red lamps advertised trade.

clue.text: Foreword to mobile, as one has ascended

blocks.note: first meaning: the word that comes before 'mobile' in the stock phrase for social climbers
second meaning: in a rising direction

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreword' looks like a book's preface, but it is literally the word placed in front of 'mobile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes motion towards higher ground, and it also opens the set phrase for people climbing the social ladder.

clue.text: Guards murphies - even TV's split inside

indicators.note: being split means broken into separate parts that go to different places
inside means within, so these letters go into the other word

blocks.note: praties is an Irish dialect word for potatoes, and murphies is a slang word for them too
taken as written
taken as written, the two letters to be separated

explanation.surface: Someone protecting their potatoes while the television set breaks apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The TV is split: its T follows the first insert, its V goes in further along. Murphies and praties are both Irish-flavoured words for potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Preventatives are measures taken to stop something happening, which is what a protective safeguard does.

clue.text: An age we took to fix - will shortly come

indicators.note: fixing something means putting it into working order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A complaint that a repair job dragged on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An age' and 'shortly' pull in opposite directions in the surface; the answer is a phrase for an event that is only days away.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying there are seven days left means the event is imminent, arriving soon.

clue.text: Got my own back up, worn in extreme youth

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to get one's own back is to repay a wrong

explanation.surface: Taking revenge while wearing something from babyhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' does double duty in the surface, as part of 'got my own back'; in the wordplay 'back up' tells you to read upwards. Diaper is the American word for a nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies wear nappies, called diapers in America, during the very earliest stage of life.

clue.text: You start too soon, though regularly planned

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of 'You'
too soon means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone jumped the gun on something scheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You start' reads as a verb phrase, but it means the beginning of the word 'You'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual recurs on a fixed schedule once every twelve months, so it is planned at regular intervals.

clue.text: Was authorising tower to be designed

indicators.note: designing means planning a new shape, so the letters are set into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An official giving permission for a tower to be planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authorising' suggests granting permission; it is being used in the literal sense of acting as an author.
explanation.definitionFit: To be authoring a text is to be writing it, so the past tense of writing fits.

clue.text: Wee dram for a Glaswegian: the rot's mended:"Who W a Z-an Othello"

annotation.answer: THERE WAS A TRAGEDIAN FROM GWELO

definitions.note: the following line of the limerick, given in abbreviated form

indicators.note: something mended has been reworked and put back together, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.clueFragment: Wee dram for a Glaswegian: the rot
blocks.note: taken as written, twenty-seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A small Scotch whisky for a man from Glasgow, as the rot is cured.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the opening line of a limerick, and the quoted part is its second line squeezed down: 'Who was a Zimbabwean Othello'. Gwelo is a town in Zimbabwe, now called Gweru.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick's first line sets up a rhyme the next line completes, so naming the second line identifies the first.

clue.text: See 10 across
Spy with black suit to dig a creature out

definitions.note: describes the tool's purpose rather than naming a noun

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
spades is one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: An undercover agent in a dark suit sent to unearth an informant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'creature' is the small burrowing animal, not a spy's quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener uses this narrow digging implement to excavate tunnels and remove burrowing animals from a lawn.

clue.text: Must be Charles II's girl, with mournful tone

blocks.note: Charles II was a king, abbreviated K
Nell Gwyn was the actress who was Charles II's famous mistress

explanation.surface: Speculation that a sad-voiced woman is the Restoration king's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn, an orange-seller turned actress, was the best-known mistress of England's King Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the slow toll of a bell rung for a death or funeral, a sorrowful sound.

clue.text: Quiz ends with cobblers' thing, a sort of mark

blocks.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on
a question mark is one sort of punctuation mark

explanation.surface: A quiz that finishes on shoemaking and punctuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is also British slang for nonsense, which colours the surface; here it means shoemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Every quiz finishes with a final query, the one that comes after all the rest.

clue.text: Friendly as will be found with hikers various

indicators.note: various means of differing kinds, so the letters take a different form

blocks.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, or as
taken as written

explanation.surface: Walkers of all kinds are found to be sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' seems to mean sociable, but the Quakers are the Religious Society of Friends, so it takes a capital-F sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Society of Friends, so being like a Quaker is being like a Friend.

clue.text: Last setter's Gilbert, Guardian of the land

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
the setter says 'I am', shortened
Bab was W. S. Gilbert's pen name, as in the Bab Ballads
the newspaper's leader column speaks as 'we'

explanation.surface: The crossword setter names Gilbert as a protector of his country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the newspaper that printed this puzzle; its editorials use the collective 'we'. The country is home to Gwelo from the limerick at 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Zimbabwe is a country in southern Africa, a nation and its territory.

clue.text: Not so! Her C17 playwright's about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: Thomas Otway was an English Restoration dramatist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contradiction, then a remark about a seventeenth-century dramatist's woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Otway wrote Venice Preserv'd; C17 stands for the seventeenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is the reverse of what was said contradicts it, rejecting the claim as wrong.

clue.text: Verse song, is it not? (Brahms, or like fellow)

indicators.note: the question mark signals that this phrase is not to be taken at face value but jumbled

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for verse
an aria is a solo song in opera
taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question about whether a piece of verse is a song, with Brahms cited as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms wrote famous sets of variations on themes by Handel, Haydn and Paganini.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer of variations on a theme, as Brahms was, can be called by this rare noun.

clue.text: Born mid Yanks' roughage, I'm not one for truth

indicators.note: mid means in the middle of, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: fiber is the American spelling of dietary fibre
B is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: Someone born among Americans disowns honesty while talking about diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Yanks are Americans, hence the US spelling FIBER rather than British fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibber tells small lies, so this person would admit to having little regard for honesty.

clue.text: Measures of love held by Jim's fellow-lover

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so it sits within the other piece

blocks.note: Jules et Jim is Truffaut's film about two friends who love the same woman
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Quantifying love within a romantic triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Truffaut's film Jules and Jim are rivals for Catherine; 'love' is zero in a tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: The joule is the SI unit of energy, so joules are units used in measurement.

clue.text: The setter's poem gets on line from phone

blocks.note: the setter says 'I am', shortened
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A crossword setter posts a poem online from his mobile.
explanation.walkthrough: i-mode was a Japanese mobile internet service, an early way of going online from a handset.
explanation.definitionFit: The service let handset users browse the web, so it was a means of internet access from mobiles.

clue.text: Prepared for shipping, sodium number (Clark)

blocks.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
six in Roman numerals
Clark Gable was the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A shipping note listing salt-like goods and an actor's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared for shipping' suggests packing goods; here shipping means ships, and a river fit for them is navigable.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterway deep and wide enough for vessels to pass is ready to carry boats.

clue.text: See 10
Sick one splits poet's game with whites and red

indicators.note: splitting something opens it up so another piece can sit in the gap

blocks.note: a bard is a poet
sick means unwell
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unwell player disrupts a poet's game of wine, white and red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whites and red' suggests wine, but English billiards uses two white cue balls and one red.
explanation.definitionFit: English billiards is played on a cloth table with three balls: two white cue balls and a red object ball.

clue.text: The Spanish front: I need some room, it's said

definitions.text: I need some room, it's said

blocks.note: el is the Spanish definite article
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A Spaniard at the front of a crowd asking for space.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'elbow room', meaning space to move freely.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase 'elbow room' means enough space, so this joint is what needs room in the saying.

clue.text: Framer of theorems will care provide

indicators.note: a framer constructs a new structure, so the letters are built into a fresh shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mathematician who devises proofs promises to look after someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase standing in for the noun: a place that will provide care.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly or convalescent residents live in such an institution and are looked after by staff.

clue.text: Fraction type: record put for start to find

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it into that place

blocks.note: to record a vote is to mark an X
find is DISCOVERY, whose start DISC is the part replaced

explanation.surface: A note about types of fraction and how to locate a record.
explanation.walkthrough: Find gives DISCOVERY; its start is DISC, itself a record, and an X goes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra a fraction is written with a numerator above a denominator, as in this general example.
